section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the Jerusalem Talmud's statement about the power of those who perform mitzvos to transform curse into blessing, and explains the precedence of "Your people" over "Israel."
section.t: And to explain this, the maamar begins with what is stated in the Jerusalem Talmud:10
"Come and see how great is the power of those who perform a mitzvah,
for every instance of 'looking' (hashkafah) in the Torah is [a language of] curse, and this [verse] is [a language of] blessing."
For through the fulfillment of the mitzvos, they transform curse into blessing.
[And following this, the maamar explains the verse:11
"But Hashem your G-d did not want to listen to Bilaam, and Hashem your G-d transformed the curse into a blessing for you, because Hashem your G-d loves you."
That it says "Hashem your G-d" three times,
as will be explained below in section 4].
And afterwards,12
it explains the two categories of "Your people" (amecha) and "Israel,"
that those who know Torah and dwell in tents are "Israel,"
and simple people who fulfill Torah and mitzvos with innocence and simplicity are "the people of Hashem"
(Your people).13
And it gives precedence to "Your people" over "Israel,"
because "greater is study that leads to action,"14
and those who perform mitzvos transform curse into blessing.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the connection between "greater is study that leads to action" and the precedence of "Your people," explaining that the unique quality of action over study is revealed specifically in the transformation of curse to blessing.
section.t: And it can be said,
that the connection of "greater is study that leads to action" to this [principle of] giving precedence to "Your people" over "Israel,"
is,
because from the fact that study is greater because15
study leads to action, it is proven that action is the main thing.16
However, this alone is not a sufficient explanation for giving precedence to "Your people"
(those who fulfill mitzvos)
over "Israel"
(those who study Torah),
for in the words of our Sages, it itself says "greater is study."
Therefore, it adds that "those who perform mitzvos transform curse into blessing,"
meaning that in this matter
(of transforming curse into blessing)
the superiority of action over study is revealed
(similar to the future era, when action will be great17).
And since the matter of "Look down... and bless" is the transformation of curse into blessing
(as above from the Jerusalem Talmud),
therefore it gives precedence to "Your people" over "Israel."
And one must understand the connection of the transformation of curse into blessing to the superiority of action.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three aspects in the verse about Bilaam, each containing "Hashem your G-d," corresponding to different levels of Divine revelation that effect the transformation of curse to blessing and the essential love for Israel.
section.t: And behold, after the maamar explains that through the fulfillment of mitzvos one transforms curse into blessing,
the maamar brings the verse "But Hashem your G-d did not want to listen to Bilaam, and Hashem your G-d transformed the curse into a blessing for you, because Hashem your G-d loves you,"
and explains,
that in this verse there are three matters.
And in each one of them it says "Hashem your G-d."18
The matter of "did not want... to listen to Bilaam" is that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not want to listen and does not hear accusations against Israel.
And this [fact] that He does not hear the accusations
(even though from the side of the attribute of judgment they have a place19)
is from the side of the attribute of mercy,
"Hashem your G-d."
And the matter of "and He transformed the curse into a blessing for you" is that intentional sins20
are transformed into merits21
[Not only are the accusers not listened to
(but the sins are not erased),
rather, atonement for sins is effected,
and beyond this,
intentional sins are transformed into merits].
And here it says "Hashem your G-d" a second time,
for the "Hashem" from which the "did not want to listen to the accusers" is drawn is the lower "Hashem,"
and in order for there to be atonement for sins,
and especially the transformation of intentional sins into merits,
it is through the drawing down of the revelation of the supernal "Hashem."22
And the matter of "because He loves you" is the essential love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel,
that even in the level above the chain of descent, regarding which it is said "For Esav is a brother to Yaakov,"23
nevertheless, "and I love Yaakov"23
specifically.
And this is "Hashem your G-d,"
for even though in the supernal "Hashem"
(the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent)
all are equal,
nevertheless,
through the revelation of the essential love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel
("because He loves you"),
even the supernal "Hashem" is "your G-d"
(of Israel)
specifically.
And after this, the maamar explains24
the reason that it gives precedence to "Your people"
(those who fulfill mitzvos)
over "Israel"
(those who study Torah),
because
[greater is study that leads to action, and]
those who perform mitzvos transform curse into blessing
(as above in section 3).
And one must understand,
for at first glance,
in order to explain the reason that it gives precedence to "Your people" over "Israel," only that "those who perform mitzvos transform curse into blessing" is relevant,
and from the fact that the maamar also brings
(also)
the explanation of the three matters in the verse "But [Hashem your G-d] did not want... to listen to Bilaam,"
it implies
that this adds explanation to the matter of giving precedence to "Your people" over "Israel."
